extracted.intended_audience: community and non-transient non-community water system operators, water system compliance officers, and State drinking water agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and specifications (content, timing, delivery, and follow-up) for public education, supplemental monitoring, consumer notification, and outreach related to lead and copper in public water systems under 40 CFR §141.85.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger and general obligations when exceeding lead action level
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that exceeds the lead action level based on tap water samples collected in accordance with § 141.86 must distribute public education materials in paragraph (a) and follow delivery requirements in paragraph (b); must offer to sample tap water for any person served who requests it; deliver consumer notices of lead and copper tap water monitoring results to persons served at sampled sites; and follow additional requirements for systems with lead/galvanized/unknown service lines, multiple exceedances, LEP populations, outreach obligations, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph establishes who is required to act (systems exceeding the lead action level) and summarizes the set of obligations spelled out in subsequent paragraphs (a)–(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content: include specified elements in written public education materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Community and non-transient non-community water systems must include the elements in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) through (vii) in written materials in the same order. Language in (a)(1)(i), (ii), and (vii) must be included exactly as written except for bracketed system-specific text. States may approve changes that are more protective of health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water systems must submit a copy of all written public education materials to the State prior to delivery; States may require pre-approval. Any additional information must be consistent with (a)(1)(i)-(vii) and in plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Important information about lead (exact notice text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials must include the specified 'Important Information About Lead in Your Drinking Water' statement identifying the system, noting elevated levels of lead in some homes/buildings, and warning that lead can cause serious health problems, especially for pregnant people and young children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This text (Figure 1 to Paragraph (a)(1)(i)) must be included exactly as written except for bracketed insertions of system-specific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Health effects of lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials must include the health effects text (Figure 2 to Paragraph (a)(1)(ii)): 'There is no safe level of lead in drinking water...' and describe effects on infants, children, pregnant people, and adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language must be included exactly as written (except bracketed system-specific text) and instruct consumers to contact their health care provider for more information about risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Sources of lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what lead is, possible sources of lead in drinking water and how lead enters drinking water (including plumbing materials, service lines, connectors), include definition of 'lead free' per SDWA section 1417, note that lead levels may vary over time, and discuss other important sources of lead (e.g., paint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This element includes subparts (A)-(C) and must make clear that a single tap sampling result may not show all exposures; incorporate system-specific details where bracketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Consumer steps to reduce lead exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss steps consumers can take to reduce exposure, including using certified filters, flushing guidance, cautions about hot water, boiling not reducing lead, cleaning faucet aerators, alternative water sources, recommending blood testing for children, and instructions on how to get water tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subpoints (A)-(H) describe recommended actions: provide filter information, flushing encouragement (longer flushing for lead/galvanized requiring replacement lines), caution about hot water for baby formula, boiling does not reduce lead, cleaning aerators, alternative water sources for vulnerable groups, directing parents to blood testing and health department contact, and how to request sampling (see paragraph (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Levels of lead in drinking water
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why there are elevated lead levels in the system's drinking water (if known) and what the water system is doing to reduce lead levels in homes/buildings in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide system-specific explanation of causes and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: Information on lead/galvanized/unknown service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems with lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines, materials must: discuss opportunities to replace such service lines; discuss opportunities to identify material of unknown lines; include how to obtain/view the service line inventory online (if required); include how to obtain/view the service line replacement plan (if required); include information on financing programs if customer payment is expected; include statement that system must replace its portion when owner notifies system of owner replacement plans; and include instructions for consumers to notify system if they disagree with material categorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems with lead connectors or connectors of unknown material, at minimum include how to obtain the service line inventory (a)(1)(vi)(C). Where customer payment is anticipated, provide information about financing assistance programs (a)(1)(vi)(E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education element: More information/contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide system contact information (name, phone or email, website) and refer consumers to EPA's lead web resources and health care providers for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Figure 3 to Paragraph (a)(1)(vii); include system contact details, website, and https://www.epa.gov/lead as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEP (Limited English Proficiency) language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems serving a large proportion of consumers with limited English proficiency (as determined by the State), all required public education materials must contain information in the appropriate language(s) about the importance of the materials and either provide info on where to obtain a translated copy or assistance in the appropriate language(s), or the materials must be in the appropriate language(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State determines when LEP requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: 60‑day delivery requirement for community systems after exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time a community water system exceeds the lead action level, the system must conduct the public education tasks in paragraph (b)(2) within 60 days after the end of the tap sampling period in which the exceedance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines end of tap sampling period: for systems on standard monitoring it is June 30 or Dec 31; for systems required to monitor annually or less frequently it is Sept 30 (or last day of State-established alternate 4-month period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery: written materials to customers and service connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver written materials meeting the content requirements of paragraph (a) to each customer receiving a bill and to other service connections to which water is delivered; for multi-family dwellings, deliver to each unit or post at a conspicuous location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery must meet coverage expectations; posting in multi-family buildings allowed instead of individual delivery when specified (see other paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting at‑risk consumers and organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact consumers most at risk by delivering education materials to local public health agencies (even if not in system service area) along with an informational notice encouraging distribution to their affected customers; water system must contact health agencies directly by phone, email, or in-person. If agencies provide lists of community-based organizations serving high-risk populations, deliver materials to organizations on those lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures outreach beyond the system boundaries to reach vulnerable populations (b)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery to specific local organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver materials that meet paragraph (a) content to organizations within the service area: schools/child care/school boards; WIC and Head Start; public and private hospitals and medical clinics; pediatricians; family planning clinics; local welfare agencies; obstetricians-gynecologists and midwives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These organizations are explicitly listed in (b)(2)(ii)(B)(1)-(7) as targets for distribution to reach populations at highest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly water-bill message requirement while exceeding action level
rubrics_metrics.description: No less often than quarterly, provide information with each water bill while the system exceeds the action level. The message must include the statement in Figure 4 exactly as written except for bracketed system-specific text. The State may allow a separate mailing if the system cannot place the information on bills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4 text: '[INSERT NAME OF WATER SYSTEM] found elevated levels of lead in drinking water in some homes/buildings. Lead can cause serious health problems. For more information please contact [INSERT NAME OF WATER SYSTEM] [or visit (INSERT WATER SYSTEM WEBSITE)].'

rubrics_metrics.name: Website posting requirement for larger systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Post material meeting paragraph (a) on the water system's website if the system serves a population greater than 50,000, and retain the material on the website for as long as the system exceeds the action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online posting is required for larger systems to ensure broad access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a press release to media outlets (newspaper, television, radio) stating the water system found elevated lead in some homes/buildings and meeting paragraph (a) content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure media outreach includes the core public education content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement additional outreach activities (choose at least three)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement at least three additional activities from categories listed in (b)(2)(vi)(A)-(J), with educational content and activity selection determined in consultation with the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories include public service announcements, paid advertisements, public area displays, emails, public meetings, household deliveries, targeted individual customer contact, direct distribution to multi-family homes/institutions, contacting plumbers/contractors, or other State-approved methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat public education activities until action level achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: A community water system must repeat the activities in paragraph (b)(2) each tap sampling period until the system is at or below the lead action level. These repeated activities must be completed within 60 days of the end of each tap sampling period. A calculated 90th percentile at or below the action level based on fewer than the minimum required samples under § 141.86 cannot be used to meet the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing repetition is required until the system remedial goals are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-transient non-community systems: poster and pamphlet requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the end of each tap sampling period with an exceedance, a non-transient non-community water system must: post informational posters on lead in drinking water in a public/common area in each building served until at/below the action level, and distribute informational pamphlets/brochures to each person served. The State may allow electronic transmission if it achieves equivalent coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and content parallel community system requirements but tailored for non-transient non-community settings (b)(4)(i)-(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small system flexibilities (systems ≤3,300 persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 3,300 or fewer persons may limit certain public education aspects: (i) for distribution to organizations listed in (b)(2)(ii), limit to facilities most likely visited by pregnant people and children; (ii) State may waive the press release requirement (b)(2)(v) if notices are distributed to every household; (iii) must implement at least one activity from (b)(2)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States can exercise flexibility for very small systems to reduce burden while targeting high-risk audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension process for completing outreach activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system may request a written extension from the State to complete specified activities (b)(2)(ii)-(vi) for community systems or (b)(4)(i)-(ii) for non-transient non-community systems. The extension must be approved in writing by the State before the 60-day deadline and may be granted case-by-case if the system demonstrates infeasibility; activities must be completed no later than six months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the exceedance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are exceptional and require State approval in advance of statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative option for certain facilities to perform reduced tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: A community water system (e.g., prison or hospital) where the population cannot make plumbing improvements and the system provides water as part of the cost of services (not separately charged) may apply to the State to perform the non-transient non-community tasks in (b)(4) and (5) in lieu of (b)(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application to the State must be in writing unless waived by the State; this recognizes settings where customers cannot take remedial steps themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supplemental tap sampling to consumers when system exceeds action level
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that exceeds the lead action level must offer to sample for lead in the tap water of any person served who requests it. At sites served by lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines, samples must capture both water in contact with premise plumbing and water in contact with the service line (e.g., first- and fifth-liter samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commitment to on-request sampling applies to any person served by the system when the system exceeds the action level (c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer sampling regardless of exceedance for properties with lead/galvanized/unknown lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must offer to sample for lead in the tap water of any person served by a lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service line who requests it, regardless of whether the system exceeds the lead action level. Samples must capture both premise plumbing and service line contact (e.g., first- and fifth-liter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures property-level access to sampling for service lines of concern even absent a system-wide exceedance (c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer notice of individual supplemental monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must provide a consumer notice of the individual tap results from supplemental tap water monitoring carried out under paragraph (c) to the persons served at the specific sampling site (e.g., occupants of the building where the tap was sampled). Notices must meet requirements of paragraphs (d)(2)-(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be tailored to the sampled site and follow the timing, content, and delivery rules in (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of consumer notification of tap results
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system must provide the consumer notice as soon as practicable but no later than three business days after the water system learns of the tap monitoring results. Notification by mail must be postmarked within three business days of learning of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast notification is required to inform consumers promptly of potential exposure (d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for consumer notice — lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer notice for lead must include the specific tap's lead result; an explanation of health effects meeting (a)(1)(ii); information on possible lead sources meeting (a)(1)(iii)(B); a list of steps consumers can take meeting (a)(1)(iv); contact information for the water system; the maximum contaminant level goal (MCLG) and the action level for lead and definitions from § 141.153(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be comprehensive, linking test result to health guidance and remedial steps (d)(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for consumer notice — copper
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer notice for copper must include the tap's copper result; an explanation of health effects as provided in appendix B to subpart Q; a list of steps consumers can take to reduce exposure to copper; contact information; and the MCLG and action level for copper and definitions from § 141.153(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead and copper notices may be combined (d)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery methods for consumer notices of tap results
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide consumer notice to persons served at the sampled tap via electronic means (email/text), by phone call/voice message, hand delivery, mail, or another State-approved method. For non-transient non-community systems the State may approve posting results in a conspicuous area. If delivered by phone/voice message, follow up with a written notice hand delivered or postmarked within 30 days of learning results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple delivery methods allowed subject to State approval; phone delivery must be supplemented by written follow-up (d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of known or potentially lead-containing service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems with lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines in their inventory must provide notification to customers and all persons served at the service connection with such a service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ties service line inventory obligations (§ 141.84) to customer notification (e)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for service-line notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide notification no later than 30 days after completion of the baseline inventory and repeat within 30 days after each annual inventory update until the service connection is no longer lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown. For new customers, provide at time of service initiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prompt, repeated notices tied to inventory updates (e)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of notification for confirmed lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must include: a statement that the service line is lead or galvanized requiring replacement; an explanation of health effects meeting (a)(1)(ii); steps persons can take meeting (a)(1)(iv); a statement that the consumer can request tap sampling per paragraph (c); info on how to obtain/view the service line replacement plan if required; information on opportunities and financing for replacement where customer payment is expected; a statement that the water system is required to replace its portion when the property owner notifies the system they are replacing their portion; and instructions for customers to notify the system if they disagree with the service line material categorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be comprehensive about status, remedies, and options (e)(3)(i)(A)-(H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of notification for lead-status-unknown service line
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must state that the service line material is unknown but may be lead, include the information required in e(3)(i)(B)–(E) (health effects, steps to reduce exposure, sampling request, how to obtain replacement plan/inventory), and provide information about opportunities to verify the material of the service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages verification/identification of service line material when unknown (e)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery methods for service-line notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the notice to customers and persons served at the service connection by mail or another State-approved method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State approval may allow alternative delivery mechanisms to ensure coverage (e)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification due to disturbance of a service line
rubrics_metrics.description: If a water system causes a disturbance to a lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service line (e.g., shut off/bypass, operating a valve, reconnecting, physical action or vibration that could dislodge pipe scale), the system must provide information about the potential for elevated lead levels arising from the disturbance. The information must include public education materials that meet (a)(1)(ii)-(iv) and (vi) and contact information, and instructions for a flushing procedure to remove particulate lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disturbance includes many operational actions; notice must include health guidance and flushing instructions (f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements when disturbance results from meter/mains replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the disturbance is from replacement of an inline water meter, meter setter, connector, or from replacement of a water main where the service line pipe is physically cut, the water system must provide the f(1) information plus a pitcher filter or certified point-of-use device to reduce lead, instructions for use, and six months of replacement cartridges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a heightened mitigation requirement for disturbances that physically cut or alter service lines (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements after disturbance for persons at service connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with paragraph (f) requirements for persons served at the service connection before any service line that was shut off or bypassed is returned to service. If there was a disturbance without shutoff/bypass, comply as soon as possible but no later than 24 hours following the disturbance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate action is required to protect those at the sampled connection (f)(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for notifying customers (property owners) after disturbance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the f(1) information to customers associated with the service connection (e.g., property owners who are not current occupants) no later than 30 days following the disturbance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows a longer timeframe for reaching property owners vs. occupants at the service connection (f)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial/full service-line replacement is not a 'disturbance' for §141.85(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that conducts a partial or full replacement of a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line must follow §141.84(h) procedures; such partial or full replacements are not considered 'disturbances' for the purposes of paragraph (f) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement work follows separate notification/mitigation rules in §141.84(h) and is excluded from the 'disturbance' provisions in (f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach activities to encourage participation in full service line replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems that do not meet the required replacement rate must conduct at least one outreach activity (from the list in (h)(2)) to discuss the mandatory replacement program and distribute public education materials meeting paragraph (a) (except (a)(1)(i) and (v)). The activity must be conducted in the year following the program year the system missed the rate and annually thereafter until goals are met or no qualifying service lines remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies continuing outreach obligations tied to replacement performance (h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed outreach activities for replacement participation (list and rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For community systems serving >3,300 persons, outreach must be one of (h)(2)(i)-(iv) or two of (h)(2)(v)-(viii). For systems ≤3,300 persons, outreach must be one of (h)(2)(i)-(viii). Activities include: conducting a public meeting; participating in community events; contacting customers by phone/text/email/door hanger; using another State-approved method; sending certified mail to customers/persons served at service connections with lead/galvanized requiring replacement service lines; conducting a social media campaign; outreach via media (newspaper/TV/radio); and visiting targeted customers to discuss replacement opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a menu of outreach options with differing requirements by system size; targeted visits and certified mail are explicitly called out (h)(2)(i)-(viii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting and public education to local/State health agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: All community water systems must provide local and State health agencies with Distribution System and Site Assessment results (including location of tap sample site exceeding 0.010 mg/L, initial and follow-up tap sample results, water quality parameter monitoring, and any distribution system management actions or corrosion control treatment adjustments) and copies of public education materials described in (a) and outreach materials described in (h). These must be sent annually for actions conducted in the previous calendar year no later than July 1 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery may be by mail, email, or another State-approved method (i)(1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements for systems with multiple lead action level exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that exceeds the lead action level at least three times in a rolling five-year period (or upon a third exceedance even if five years have not elapsed) must conduct the activities in paragraph (j). The first rolling five-year period begins on the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers enhanced mitigation and monitoring when exceedances are recurrent (j)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of filters and cartridges after multiple exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 60 days after the tap sampling period in which a system meets the criteria of j(1) (three exceedances in a rolling five-year period), the system must make available to all consumers pitcher filters or certified point-of-use devices to reduce lead, six months of replacement cartridges, and instructions for use. The system must continue to make replacement cartridges available until it may discontinue actions under later subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consumer-level mitigation (filters + cartridges) is mandated upon repeated exceedances (j)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter plan submission after second exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 60 days after a system exceeds the lead action level for the second time in a rolling five-year period, the system must submit a filter plan to the State. The State must review and approve the plan within 60 days. If the system later meets the three-exceedance criteria, it is not required to re-submit the plan unless it updates the plan or the State requests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires near-term planning for consumer filtration after repeat exceedances, with defined State review timelines (j)(3).
